title: Progressive coordination and mutual exclusion
description:
## Objective

Extend Kanbus with optional coordination for distributed workers, without compromising the core property: Kanbus must continue to work using Git alone. MQTT and a Mutex API are progressive enhancement, not dependencies.

This is initially motivated by Spoticus (one scheduler epoch, one dispatch decision) and by local-first / cloud-backstop workers (for example TTS), but it must be a generic Kanbus capability. Spoticus must not dictate the architecture.

## Constraint versus Beads exclusive claim

Kanbus already has `kbs update --claim` (assignee + `in_progress`). That is not a mutex.

The README currently says exclusive claiming was removed because it does not align with distributed Git. This initiative does **not** reverse that: Git-only installs stay fully functional, and duplicate work remains possible at Level 1. We add an optional claim/lease layer on top, with stronger guarantees only when extra infrastructure is configured.

## Three levels

1. **Git (required):** Durable source of truth. Soft-lease via the issue/event model. Contention windows must tolerate Git latency. A Git-only installation is legitimate, not broken.
2. **MQTT (optional):** Kanbus already has optional MQTT gossip/overlay (`docs/REALTIME.md`). Fast-path CLAIM → contention window (seconds) → deterministic tie-break → LEASE / renew / RELEASE. Soft mutex only; partitions can still duplicate.
3. **Mutex API (optional):** Hard arbitration. Atomically create/claim resource X iff nobody currently owns X. Proposed shape: API Gateway REST → direct DynamoDB conditional write. No Lambda. No AppSync. Workers authenticate to the Kanbus Mutex API; they do not get the AWS account. DynamoDB holds only live leases (resource_id, owner_id, claim_id, revision, claimed_at, expires_at), not Kanbus history. TTL garbage-collects abandoned leases.

A worker asks Kanbus to claim a resource. Kanbus uses the strongest configured provider. Business logic does not fork per transport.

## Protocol (define first, Gherkin source of truth)

One transport-independent claim/lease protocol: resource identity, owner identity, claim IDs, contention behavior, lease TTLs and renewals, expiration, release/completion, deterministic collision resolution, revision semantics, and failure behavior. Then implement Git lease → MQTT fast-path → optional hard-mutex provider. Dual-runtime (Python + Rust) after Gherkin; no Python-only or Rust-only PRs.

## Revision-aware results

Publication is by logical task revision, not whoever finishes last. An obsolete local render must not overwrite a newer revision. Pattern: local-first → wait → cloud backstop, without making the cloud the queue or source of truth.

## Out of scope

This is not a second queue competing with Kanbus. Durable history stays in Git. DynamoDB is ephemeral coordination state only.

comments.text:
Product brief from Ryan, 2026-09-14. Working contract is the initiative description; this comment is the source brief.

# Progressive Coordination and Mutual Exclusion for Kanbus

Kanbus must continue to work using Git alone. MQTT and a Mutex API are progressive enhancement, not dependencies. Generic Kanbus capability (Spoticus is a motivating consumer, not the architecture owner).

Three levels: (1) Git soft-lease via issue/event model, Git latency; (2) MQTT CLAIM → contention window → tie-break → LEASE/renew/RELEASE, soft mutex; (3) Mutex API = API Gateway REST → direct DynamoDB conditional write, no Lambda, no AppSync. DynamoDB holds only live leases. Worker asks Kanbus to claim; Kanbus uses strongest configured provider.

Protocol first (Gherkin): resource/owner/claim IDs, contention vs TTL, renew, expire, release, deterministic collision, revision-aware publish, failure. Then Git → MQTT → optional hard mutex. Dual-runtime after Gherkin.

Not a second queue. Durable history stays in Git.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Initiative is actively underway: Level 1 Git soft leases and Level 2 MQTT soft leases are implemented in both runtimes; the Level 3 Mutex API stack/client is implemented and deployed. Remaining work is to reconcile production validation evidence, measure request cost, and complete isolated multi-router hard-lease validation. GitHub webhooks are a separate future integration, not a prerequisite for this initiative.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Complete. Level 1 (Git soft lease) and Level 2 (MQTT soft lease) are implemented in both runtimes; Level 3 (Mutex API on API Gateway plus DynamoDB, no Lambda in the lease path) is deployed with dual-runtime clients (kbs-b6c014). Isolated multi-router hard-lease validation is now recorded live: exactly-one-start contention, expiry takeover and soft-duplicate behavior (kbs-c77a6b, kbs-63679c). Follow-ups tracked separately: kbs-357ca6 (request-cost measurement) and kbs-7d2e34 (long-lived revocable Mutex tokens).
